limits: One run per task per arm; these are regression and discovery runs, not statistical evidence of higher general model accuracy.
Bash has the same four matched tasks in two batches, plus a successful real Qwen one-shot smoke test.
Heavy concurrent host load invalidates speed comparisons; the captured-output EOF regression is independent of speed.

The first final parser run completed its task but the wall clock jumped about 358 seconds; the Date.now-based driver then timed it out. That failed driver result is preserved and a repeat uses monotonic deadlines. Legacy wall_seconds fields are measured by the runner with time.monotonic().
RPC text checks and deterministic installed-TUI renderer checks are separate evidence.
External MCP is disabled by project policy and was not exercised.
The optional analysis Python environment was not installed; model tasks used system Python or project virtualenvs.
The child scratch guard targets observed direct commands against .pi/tmp/venv; it is not exhaustive shell ownership enforcement.

The development installs omit the optional analysis environment. Some model runs tried unavailable commands or global pip before recovering with a project virtualenv; those tool errors remain in the recorded counts.

The final monotonic-driver parser repeat still accepted 25:00:00 and failed its functional check despite receiving changing-code guidance. General Qwen coding accuracy is not demonstrated to exceed the Bash baseline.
